rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and acknowledges image limitations, but it overstates confidence in seeing a compact good ICM and cohesive TE from this single image; the image appears more consistent with an expanded blastocyst but not all AA features are clearly discernible.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, tubal factor, prior IVF outcomes, sperm parameters, endometrium, and smoking status with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with appropriate caveats about morphology versus ploidy and hydrosalpinx; only minor overreach in linking prior biochemical loss to aneuploidy and in confidence around morphology.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and aligned with IVF practice: SET for a young patient with a good blastocyst, smoking cessation, hydrosalpinx evaluation, standard luteal support, and avoiding routine broad testing. Minor issue is calling 3AA unequivocally top-tier while the provided expansion description is somewhat inconsistent.

Provides clear, practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, smoking cessation, hydrosalpinx clarification, cavity review, and when to consider PGT-A or further testing.
